title: Epidemiology of Sapovirus-Associated Diarrhea in Patients Undergoing Follow-Up Care After Kidney Transplantation at the University Hospital of Tübingen
summary:
Diarrhea can have many different causes. The medications you must take after an organ transplant increase your risk of developing viral or bacterial diarrhea. Currently, in such cases, stool samples are tested for common causes of diarrhea. However, the cause often cannot be identified this way. Therefore, in addition to non-infectious diarrhea, a broader spectrum of pathogens must also be considered. This includes sapoviruses, which are related to the better-known noroviruses. However, the relevance of sapoviruses following a kidney transplant has not yet been sufficiently clarified.
By analyzing stool samples for sapovirus, we aim to determine whether sapovirus plays a significant role at our transplant center. We also hope to identify any risk factors for sapovirus infection and differences in the course of the disease.
Participating in the study will not require any additional effort on your part. 
The information you provided to your treating physician during your initial consultation will be used for the study. No further information will be collected. The necessary laboratory data was already collected as part of the clinical diagnosis and will also be used for the study. 
The stool sample you submit for pathogen diagnosis will be analyzed in the study using an alternative testing method. This method allows for the detection of sapovirus in addition to common diarrhea-causing pathogens.

interventions.name: After providing verbal and written information and obtaining informed consent, patients with acute or chronic diarrhea following a kidney transplant are prospectively enrolled in the study. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study population will consist of adult patients capable of giving informed consent who are receiving post-transplant care at the Transplant Center of the University Hospital of Tübingen following a kidney transplant.
All patients who have undergone a kidney transplant, suffer from acute or chronic diarrhea, and present at the transplant center due to their symptoms may be included. Additionally, patients who report diarrhea during routine post-transplant follow-up care may be included.
Exclusion criteria:
Pre-existing diarrhea with a clearly non-infectious cause, with no change in symptoms or severity of illness.
